context: A teacher and a teen discuss a world history project
purpose: Teach: 女王/外来/航海/南米/無名/無数/メタ/語彙

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 桜さん、自由研究、女王の時代の南米遠征、難しいテーマね。
lines.en: Sakura, a free research project on South American expeditions during the colonial era — that's quite an ambitious topic.
lines.style: Warm, thoughtful opening. Slight lean-in. Acknowledges the difficulty without discouraging. Measured pace, teacher's genuine interest in the scope of the work.

lines.speaker: sakura_teen
lines.jp: はい。外来文化との接触、無数の影響を残しました。
lines.en: Yes. The contact with foreign cultures left countless impacts that shaped entire societies.
lines.style: Steady, measured. Sakura thinking aloud, testing the scope of her own project. Not defensive — genuine intellectual engagement. Slight pause before 'countless' as she considers the scale.

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 当時の航海記録、無名の書記官の手によるものも残っています。
lines.en: There are period voyage records from that time too — some written by nameless clerks whose accounts survived.
lines.style: Leaning forward slightly. Genuine excitement at sharing a research lead. Warm, conspiratorial tone — offering Sakura a real resource. Voice quickens on the specifics, slows on 'survived'.

lines.speaker: sakura_teen
lines.jp: メタ的に分類する論文も、図書館にあるそうです。
lines.en: There are papers in the library that classify these sources—breaking down the different layers and contexts.
lines.style: Testing Asuka's reaction. Slight edge of showing she's already thinking ahead. Not quite confident — probing to see if this direction is right. Quieter at the end.

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 当時の語彙、現代と意味が違うところ、丁寧に確認してくださいね。
lines.en: Right — and make sure you're careful about period vocabulary. The meanings shift so much from then to now. Check those definitions closely.
lines.style: Gentle but firm directive. Not lecturing — guiding. Slight emphasis on 'careful' and 'closely', voice steadies into quiet authority. Teacher's protective attention to detail.
